cards.text: Let's head to Caesarea, friend, where a man named Cornelius is a centurion in what was called the Italian Regiment. That's a man with soldiers taking his orders. Back in the junk drawer, the only thing taking MY orders was a twist tie, and it ignored me.
And this soldier loves God, friend. He and all his household are devout and God-fearing, and his faith doesn't stay inside his own house.

cards.question: Cornelius is devout and God-fearing. How does his faith show up in his life?

answers.text: He gives generously to the people and prays regularly
He fasts often and keeps every feast in Jerusalem
He studies the law with the priests every week

cards.text: One day at about the ninth hour, an angel of God comes to Cornelius in a clear vision and says, “Cornelius!” Friend, if I heard my name like that, I'd drop every cookie in the room.

cards.question: When the angel calls his name, how does Cornelius react?

answers.text: He stares at him in fear
He runs out of the room

cards.text: Cornelius asks, “What is it, Lord?” And the angel answers with news about his prayers and his gifts to the poor.

cards.question: What does the angel say Cornelius's prayers and gifts to the poor have done?

answers.text: Gone up as a memorial offering before God
Paid for every wrong he has ever done
Been written down by the temple priests

cards.text: Then the angel gives Cornelius a job: send men to Joppa to call for someone.

cards.question: Who does the angel tell Cornelius to send for in Joppa?

cards.text: Here's the funny part: Peter is staying with ANOTHER Simon, so that house has two Simons in it. Somebody yells “Simon!” and two grown men turn around.

cards.question: Peter is staying with Simon the ___, whose house is by the ___.

cards.text: The angel leaves, and Cornelius has a job to hand out. He's a centurion, friend, so handing out jobs is basically his whole day.

cards.question: Who does Cornelius call in for the trip to Joppa?

answers.text: Two servants and a devout soldier
His wife and his two sons

cards.question: Cornelius sends the men to Joppa without telling them what happened.

cards.text: The next day at about the sixth hour, Cornelius's men are getting close to Joppa. Meanwhile, Peter goes up on the roof.

cards.question: Why does Peter go up on the roof?

cards.text: Up there, Peter gets hungry and wants something to eat, and the meal is being prepared. Waiting while you're hungry? I've stared down an oven timer like it owed me money.

cards.question: While the meal is being prepared, what happens to Peter?

answers.text: He walks out to the seashore
He goes down to help Simon

cards.text: Peter sees heaven open, and something like a large sheet is being let down to earth by its four corners. In the drawer, the only thing that ever came down from above was a takeout menu landing on my FACE.

cards.question: What's inside the sheet coming down to Peter?

answers.text: All kinds of animals and reptiles and birds
Stone tablets with the law written on them
Scrolls from the prophets of Israel

cards.text: Then a voice said to him: “Get up, Peter, kill and eat!” Me when I'm hungry? I'll grab a cookie off the rack so hot it singes my mustache.

cards.question: What does Peter say back to the voice?

answers.text: No Lord I have never eaten anything unclean
Yes Lord I will eat whatever is here
Wait Lord let me ask the others first

cards.question: Speaking a second time, the voice tells Peter not to call anything ___ that God has made ___.

cards.text: This happens three times, and then all at once the sheet is taken back up into heaven. THREE times, friend, and I bet Peter's stomach was voting yes every single round.

cards.question: Peter understands what the vision means right away.

cards.text: While Peter is puzzling over it, Cornelius's men find Simon's house and come to the gate. They call out to ask if Simon called Peter is staying there, and good thing they said WHICH Simon.

cards.question: Peter is still thinking about the vision. Who tells him that three men are looking for him?
The Spirit tells Peter to go downstairs and go with the three men without hesitation. Why?

answers.text: Because they are old friends of Peter

cards.text: So Peter goes down and says, “Here am I, the one you are looking for. Why have you come?” The Spirit gave him a heads-up, so he's READY, and me, I've been ambushed by my OWN oven timer.

cards.question: The men tell Peter that Cornelius has a good reputation among the whole Jewish nation.
According to Cornelius's men, what did a holy angel tell Cornelius to do?

answers.text: Bring Peter to his home to hear his message
Bring Peter to Caesarea to stand trial
Bring Peter to pray over his soldiers

cards.question: Peter invites Cornelius's men in as his guests. What does Peter do the next day?

answers.text: Goes with them and some brothers from Joppa
Sends them home with a letter for Cornelius
Stays in Joppa to keep praying on the roof

cards.text: Hold onto your apron, friend, because this story is only getting started.

findings.problem: "This soldier loves God" renames what the text says. Acts 10:2 calls Cornelius "devout and God-fearing." It never says he loves God.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Peter shows up here for the first time, with Simon called Peter named only in the answer to card 9. No card says who he is, such as one of Jesus's apostles.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The blanks "tanner" and "sea" test wording the baker hasn't seen. Card 10 gives nothing to reason from, so the pick is luck.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "Up there, Peter gets hungry…", "Waiting while you're hungry?" and "I've stared down an oven timer…"

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quoted voice, "Me when I'm hungry?" and "I'll grab a cookie off the rack…"

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The final story card holds only the line saying the story isn't over and tells no verse, but it cites Acts 10:23. Card 18 already covers that verse.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-isn't-over line and tells no verse, what should its "verses" field hold: the passage's last verse, an empty value, or something else?
